findings.problem: Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124 (Reporting Adverse Events) covers an adverse event after administration that results from a dispensing error or is a serious adverse drug event. It states that the pharmacist or pharmacy intern 'remains responsible for reporting the event to the Board of Registration in Pharmacy, in accordance with Board regulations'. 247 CMR 20.02(1)-(2) and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D(b)-(c) put the filing duty on the Manager of Record, and the duty to notify DPH on the pharmacy. The texts therefore leave open what the administering pharmacist's or intern's continuing responsibility consists of. The section does not treat this as open. It settles it in the negative: the worked example says flatly that 'the intern is not the one who files', and common_traps[21] makes it a trap to name the administering pharmacist or intern as the one who must file. It gives the administering pharmacist or intern no safe course.
findings.rationale: The accurate part should stay. Under 247 CMR 20.02 the Manager of Record files, and no Board rule names the administering individual; 247 CMR 9.00 has no individual reporting duty either. But the Department's guidance names the administering pharmacist or pharmacy intern in terms, and the section's own quick_review[18] repeats that sentence. A flat negative, with the circular's own actor labelled a trap, tells a candidate on Massachusetts facts that the person who gave the injection has no Board-reporting responsibility. The Department's express statement cuts against that, and a question built on the circular would expect the opposite answer. The fix is small. Present the tension as a point the texts leave open: the rule gives the filing to the Manager of Record, while the circular says the administering pharmacist or intern remains responsible for the report. Then give a safe course, for example that the administering pharmacist or intern makes sure the event reaches the Manager of Record at once and that the Board report is made within the period, instead of the bare 'the intern is not the one who files'. Recast common_traps[21] so that it does not mark the circular's named actor as an error.

authorities.exact_section: Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124, Reporting Adverse Events, final paragraph

findings.problem: The section says a serious adverse drug event from a listed medication that was not manufactured, produced or compounded at the pharmacy, with no improper dispensing, 'is not reportable under either' 247 CMR 20.02 or s. 39D. It sets this beside the circular's statement that the pharmacist or intern remains responsible for reporting a serious adverse drug event to the Board, without saying that the rule is narrower than that sentence.
findings.rationale: The literal words of 247 CMR 20.02(2) and s. 39D(c) do support the limitation, so the statement is correct about the mandatory reach of the Board rule and statute. It would read more safely as 'not required by 247 CMR 20.02(2) or s. 39D(c)', with a note that the circular's sentence appears to contemplate Board reporting of any serious adverse drug event and that voluntary MedWatch reporting remains open. Low, because the statement has textual support.

authorities.exact_section: Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124, Reporting Adverse Events

findings.problem: The section describes 21 CFR 1306.07(a) as permitting a Schedule II narcotic for maintenance or detoxification 'only if separately registered with DEA as a narcotic treatment program'. It does not mention paragraph (b), which lets a practitioner who is not an NTP dispense (but not prescribe) up to a three-day supply at one time while arranging referral. Nor does it mention paragraph (c), which covers hospital administration or dispensing as an incidental adjunct and cases of intractable pain.
findings.rationale: As a description of the condition in paragraph (a) the wording is accurate. The section's conclusions are correct: no paragraph of 1306.07 provides for prescribing methadone for maintenance or detoxification, and the order-only OTP route stands. The section also sends the full federal rules to another section. Still, the unqualified 'only' can suggest that a non-NTP practitioner may never dispense or administer a Schedule II narcotic for these purposes. A clause noting the (b) and (c) exceptions, or a cross-reference that names them, would remove that reading.

247 CMR 9.00 (searched for any individual pharmacist duty to report dispensing errors or adverse drug events to the Board; none found)

results.summary: I checked the section against the current official texts, and it is accurate almost throughout. It is accurate on the M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 1 definition of Administer (clause (c) and how each of its three routes is gated), on the s. 9(a) pharmacist entry and its 'as limited by' words, and on 105 CMR 700.004(B)(9)(a)-(e), (B)(6) and 700.003(F) in the current 2024 PDF. It is also accurate on every heading of Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124: the list and its scope, conditions (a)-(f), the OTP note, reassessment, training, CPR and competency, counseling, records, the should/must split for adverse events, the notation and communication items, and privacy, all with the circular's own modality. The same holds for 247 CMR 20.02, M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D(b)-(c) and 21 CFR 1306.07. It rightly reads the eligible list as closing only the circular's own pathway, and its safe courses on age and on meeting both the statutory and circular conditions are sound. One Medium defect calls for a minor edit. The circular says the administering pharmacist or intern 'remains responsible' for reporting to the Board; 247 CMR 20.02 has the Manager of Record file. The section turns that open tension into a flat negative ('the intern is not the one who files'), labels the circular's named actor a common trap, and gives no safe course. There are two Low points: the 'not reportable' phrasing for a serious adverse drug event from a drug not made at the pharmacy, and the unqualified 'only' for 1306.07(a) with no mention of (b) or (c). All six mapped practice questions can be answered from the section, and none is contradicted by it.
